react_inline_caveats.js-cache-function-results.md: Cache only pure non-sensitive computations; bound any Map and define invalidation. The cookie-presence example is a UI hint, not authentication, and must never authorize an action.
react_inline_caveats.js-cache-storage.md: Browser-only examples: guard SSR and catch storage failures; invalidate cookie cache on relevant changes, and handle storage events with null keys (clear). Never cache credentials or auth decisions.
react_inline_caveats.rerender-lazy-state-init.md: Initializers must be pure and may run twice in development Strict Mode. Storage access requires browser guards, exception handling and deterministic SSR/hydration behavior. Initial props do not automatically resynchronize state.
react_inline_caveats.rendering-hydration-no-flicker.md: The raw inline-script example is not universally hydration-safe. Prefer the project/framework established theme solution, allowlist theme values, preserve a restrictive CSP with an approved nonce/hash, and never interpolate untrusted data. Do not use this for authentication state. DOM mutation can still mismatch React expectations.
react_inline_caveats.bundle-defer-third-party.md: Next.js App Router: ssr:false belongs in a Client Component wrapper, not a Server Component root layout. Keep layout server-side and render an approved existing client wrapper. Do not add analytics or a vendor service merely to optimize it.
react_inline_caveats.bundle-dynamic-imports.md: Next.js App Router: ssr:false must be declared inside a Client Component (use client), not a Server Component. Confirm router and version behavior.
react_inline_caveats.bundle-conditional.md: A typeof window guard prevents execution on the server, not necessarily bundling/tracing. Verify actual build behavior rather than assuming server bundle exclusion.
react_inline_caveats.bundle-preload.md: A typeof window guard alone does not guarantee exclusion from server bundles; prefetch can consume bandwidth and execute module initialization. Follow network approval and consent boundaries.
react_inline_caveats.js-flatmap-filter.md: flatMap still creates callback result arrays and may preserve empty strings that filter(Boolean) removed. It is not universally equivalent or allocation-free; use a single loop when avoiding allocation matters and preserve the original predicate semantics.
react_inline_caveats.rendering-script-defer-async.md: Next.js beforeInteractive placement is router/version-specific and typically restricted to root layout or document. Consult version-matched docs and preserve CSP/consent requirements.
react_inline_caveats.js-request-idle-callback.md: Idle callbacks are best-effort and may never run before page termination; timeout does not guarantee delivery within two seconds. Do not use for required audit/security work. The simple fallback does not provide IdleDeadline to chunking callbacks.

postgres_inline_caveats.security-rls-performance.md: SECURITY DEFINER uses owner privileges; RLS bypass depends on ownership, FORCE RLS and BYPASSRLS. The shown revocation also removes EXECUTE from authenticated callers, so the policy may fail: deliberately grant only required helper execution to the intended policy role after reviewing the private schema and threat model. A helper correlated on team_id can execute per distinct row value; wrapping it in SELECT does not guarantee one execution per statement.
postgres_inline_caveats.schema-constraints.md: Scope every pg_constraint existence check by both conname AND conrelid (schema-qualified table). Catalog checks do not make concurrent DDL race-free or verify an existing constraint has the required definition; serialize migrations and compare definitions. Review locking and validation cost.
postgres_inline_caveats.schema-primary-keys.md: Do not install pg_uuidv7 automatically. PostgreSQL 18+ has native uuidv7(); older installations need an explicitly approved already available generator or an existing application strategy. UUIDv4 remains appropriate where its trade-offs are acceptable. Text time-prefixed UUIDs are not standard UUIDv7/ULID and increase storage; none guarantee zero fragmentation.
postgres_inline_caveats.monitor-explain-analyze.md: Start with supplied plans or plain EXPLAIN. ANALYZE executes the statement; never analyze writes, writable CTEs or side-effecting functions. A sequential scan is not automatically wrong; inspect selectivity, table size, statistics, buffers and total workload before changing indexes or memory.
postgres_inline_caveats.monitor-pg-stat-statements.md: Check extension availability and PostgreSQL configuration offline first. Creating this extension may require shared_preload_libraries and a restart. Statistics resets mutate shared diagnostic state and require separate exact-target approval. Query text may contain sensitive values; redact output.
postgres_inline_caveats.conn-prepared-statements.md: Ports are deployment-specific, not Postgres defaults. Newer PgBouncer versions can track protocol prepared statements when configured; SQL PREPARE remains distinct. Verify actual driver and pooler versions and settings instead of blanket disabling features.
postgres_inline_caveats.conn-pooling.md: The CPU/spindle formula and memory figures are starting illustrations, not capacity guarantees. Modern pooler support for prepared statements varies by version and configuration; choose pooling mode from actual session feature requirements.
postgres_inline_caveats.data-batch-inserts.md: COPY FROM a path reads on the database SERVER, not the Windows client. For an approved local client file use an existing driver streaming facility or explicitly approved psql client-side copy; validate actual quoted Windows paths, permissions, encoding and target. Do not treat /path/to/data.csv as a local path.
postgres_inline_caveats.query-covering-indexes.md: Index-only scans still require heap visibility checks unless visibility-map state permits skipping them. INCLUDE increases index size/write costs; it does not guarantee no heap fetches.
postgres_inline_caveats.data-pagination.md: Keyset pagination avoids scanning a growing offset; cost is generally index lookup plus page retrieval, not literal O(1). Require stable unique ordering, matching index and defined null/tie handling.
postgres_inline_caveats.advanced-full-text-search.md: Leading-wildcard LIKE can use an appropriate approved pg_trgm index; full-text token search changes semantics and is not a drop-in substring replacement. Choose language/configuration explicitly and parse untrusted search input safely (for example version-supported websearch_to_tsquery).
postgres_inline_caveats.lock-short-transactions.md: Payment/API calls outside a transaction need established idempotency and reconciliation; a successful external charge and failed local update are not atomic. SET LOCAL lasts for the current transaction, not an entire session.
postgres_inline_caveats.lock-advisory.md: Prefer transaction-scoped locks under transaction pooling. Session locks require reliable same-session release in finally/error paths; a try-lock success must be unlocked. hashtext can collide. The application-control-flow block is pseudocode, not executable SQL.
